headline: Fused graph and pretrained encoders predict molecular and biomolecular properties
label: Learned Biomolecular Property Prediction
summary: Recent preprints and a January 2026 publication add explicit interaction across representations to encoder-predictor pipelines for property prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is an encoder feeding a supervised predictor, with explicit interaction across representations rather than a single embedding. XIMP passes messages across molecular graph, junction-tree, and pharmacophore abstractions, and GPCR-Filter fuses ESM-3 receptor embeddings with graph neural network ligand encodings via attention. DMG-PPI models similarity and complementarity in protein-protein interaction networks through dual channels, and TurboGAE applies subgraph-level tokenization with multimodal fusion in a graph autoencoder. RAG-GNN fuses graph embeddings with retrieved literature knowledge for functional clustering. Representation design is also targeted directly: PCEvo learns from virtual chemical edit paths under a path-consistency objective. Targets remain heterogeneous, spanning molecular properties, GPCR modulators, antibody function, and protein interaction networks, so the shared element is architectural rather than task-specific.
